value: Between the principal focus and twice the focal length (between F and 2F)
reasoning: For a convex lens the image is real and magnified only when the object lies between the focus and the centre of curvature; the image then forms beyond twice the focal length on the other side. An object at twice the focal length gives a real image of the same size, and an object beyond that gives a real but diminished image.
Inside a long current-carrying solenoid the magnetic field is uniform in magnitude and direction at every point of the cross-section, so the field lines run as parallel straight lines along the axis.

value: Slows down and bends towards the normal
reasoning: A denser medium has a higher refractive index, so light travels more slowly in it; by Snell's law the reduced speed makes the refracted ray bend towards the normal.
Resistance is directly proportional to length, so halving the nichrome wire halves its resistance; with the cell's voltage unchanged, the current given by I = V/R becomes twice its original value.

value: Pressure is larger while standing than while lying
reasoning: Pressure is thrust per unit area, and the weight of the body is the same in both postures; standing puts that weight on the small area of the feet, so the pressure on the sand is greater than when the body lies down over a large area.

value: 0 m after 1 minute and 100 m after 10 s
reasoning: One round takes 20 s, so in 60 s the athlete completes exactly three rounds and returns to the start, giving zero displacement; in 10 s only half a round is covered, ending diametrically opposite the start, so the displacement equals the diameter, 100 m.

Universal indicator is indeed a blend of several indicators and it takes different colours at different hydrogen-ion concentrations, which is how it reports pH. It is not used to find the end point in a titration, where a single indicator with a sharp colour change such as phenolphthalein or methyl orange is required.

In graphite each carbon uses only three of its four valence electrons in bonding, leaving one delocalised electron per atom free to move, so it conducts. Diamond has all four electrons locked in a rigid tetrahedral network and fullerene is a molecular solid, so neither is a good conductor.

Carbon is a minor crustal constituent, present chiefly as carbonates and coal, with a crustal abundance of roughly two hundredths of one per cent by mass. The value printed in textbooks is usually quoted as about 0.02 per cent, which matches this figure most closely among the choices offered.

Copper exposed to air containing moisture and carbon dioxide slowly acquires a green layer of basic copper carbonate; the oxides of copper are black or red, and copper sulphate needs sulphuric acid rather than carbon dioxide.

Roasting is the strong heating of a sulphide ore in a plentiful supply of air to convert it into the oxide; calcination is the corresponding heating of carbonate ores in limited air, and smelting is the later reduction of the oxide to the metal.
Solder is an alloy of lead and tin, and its low melting point is what allows it to be used for joining electrical wires.

value: The decrease in energy available at successively higher trophic levels
reasoning: Only about ten per cent of the energy at one trophic level is passed to the next, so after four or five levels too little energy remains to support a further population of consumers.
The cross TT x tt gives an entirely Tt first generation, and selfing that generation yields genotypes in the ratio 1 TT : 2 Tt : 1 tt, so pure tall plants and short plants occur equally often.

value: The claim that all variations in a species have equal chances of survival is untrue
reasoning: Survival depends on how well a particular variant suits the prevailing environment, so different variations have different chances of persisting; that selective effect is the basis of evolution. The other statements about asexual reproduction, genetic change and environmental selection are all correct.

value: A group of organisms of one species living in the same area at the same time
reasoning: A population is defined by one species sharing one place at one time; a group drawn from more than one species is a community, and a unit combining living and non-living components is an ecosystem.

value: Oxygenated blood reaches the left side of the heart from the lungs
reasoning: In double circulation the right side of the heart sends deoxygenated blood to the lungs, and the pulmonary veins return the oxygenated blood to the left atrium, from where the left ventricle pumps it to the body.

Saprophytic organisms secrete digestive enzymes onto the food material, break it down outside the body and then absorb the soluble products, which is exactly how these fungi feed. The other groupings contain parasites and organisms that ingest food into the body before digesting it.
The speed of the wave is frequency times wavelength, that is 4000 Hz multiplied by 0.30 m, giving 1200 m/s; dividing the 2400 m path by that speed gives two seconds.
Electrical power is the product of potential difference and current, so 110 V times 0.2 A gives 22 W.

value: The change in the speed of light between the two media
reasoning: Light travels at different speeds in media of different optical density, and it is this change in speed at the boundary that makes the ray change direction.
Starting from rest the change in speed is 20 km/h over ten minutes, which is one-sixth of an hour; dividing 20 by one-sixth gives an acceleration of 120 km/h squared.
In the activity series magnesium lies above aluminium, which lies above zinc, which lies above iron, so this is the order in which these metals displace hydrogen from dilute hydrochloric acid.
The stinging hairs of the nettle leaf inject methanoic acid, which is why rubbing the area with a leaf of the dock plant, containing a base, relieves the pain.

An alkali is by definition a base that dissolves in water, so all alkalis are water-soluble and they are soapy to the touch, bitter and corrosive. The first statement inverts the relationship, since many bases such as copper oxide are insoluble and therefore not alkalis.
Anhydrous calcium chloride is the drying agent packed in the guard tube, because it absorbs moisture without reacting with the hydrogen chloride gas being collected.

Fertilizers are manufactured to supply the major nutrients nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium; micronutrients such as iron are not normally part of them and are supplied instead by manures or the soil itself.

Jointed appendages are the defining feature of arthropods, the phylum to which insects belong; an earthworm is an annelid with no legs at all. Segmentation, a cylindrical body and bilateral symmetry occur in both animals and so cannot separate them.

Protochordates are marine, bilaterally symmetrical and coelomate and possess a notochord at some stage, but the notochord is never replaced by a vertebral column, which is what distinguishes them from the vertebrates.

value: At the base of the leaves or of the internodes
reasoning: Intercalary meristem is the tissue left behind between permanent tissues, lying at the base of leaves or above the nodes, and its activity is what lets grasses regrow after grazing. Apical meristem occupies the tips and lateral meristem the sides of stems and roots.
